samples.summary: The only test for the `doc` (Tree) copy arm is vacuous — it uses an empty source root and asserts `targetRoot.content` is merely defined
samples.evidence: `it('routes a doc through the Tree serializer rather than a JSON snapshot')` builds the service with `sourceRoot: {}`. In that case `readDocsRoot({})` returns `{ blocks: [] }` (docs-tree.ts:427-431, the `!tree` early return) and `writeDocsRoot` then unconditionally does `root.content = new Tree({type:'doc',children: []})` (docs-tree.ts:524-528). So `targetRoot.content` is defined no matter what was read from the source — the assertion holds even if the read step returned nothing at all, or if the source content were dropped entirely. No test anywhere copies an actual docs document (blocks/inlines/pageSetup/stylesJson) from source to target, so the 'doc' content-transfer behaviour is effectively uncovered while appearing covered.

samples.summary: The `note` branch of `copyContent` has no test at all
samples.evidence: `copyContent` has three arms: 'doc', 'note', and the JSON-root set. The spec covers 'sheet' (JSON), 'doc' (weakly), and 'pdf' (no CRDT), but never invokes `service.copy` with `type: 'note'`. Nothing asserts `readNoteRoot`/`writeNoteRoot` are used or that the note's markdown reaches the target — a regression that copied notes as empty (or crashed on the note prefix) would ship green.

samples.summary: New frontend `copyDocument` API function and the whole "Make a copy" UI wiring ship with no test
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.test.ts` covers `moveDocuments` and `deleteDocuments` (method/URL/body assertions) but has no `copyDocument` case — grep for 'copy' in that file returns nothing. Grep for 'copyDocument'/'Make a copy' across packages/frontend matches only `src/api/documents.ts` and `src/app/documents/document-list.tsx`, i.e. no test file. So the POST verb/URL, the sequential bulk loop, the singular/plural toast, and the deliberate `onSettled` (rather than `onSuccess`) refetch on partial failure — all called out as intentional in the comments — are unverified.

samples.summary: No test for copying a document that lives at the workspace root (`folderId: null`)
samples.evidence: `copy` conditionally omits the `folder: { connect }` payload when `source.folderId` is falsy, and queries siblings with `folderId: null`. Every spec case uses `SOURCE` with `folderId: 'fld-1'`; nothing exercises the null branch, so a copy of a root-level document creating a dangling/omitted folder link, or scoping siblings wrongly, is untested.

samples.summary: The blob cleanup inside the content-copy failure path is never asserted
samples.evidence: The second catch calls both `deleteDocument` and `discardBlob(fileId)`. The test 'rolls back the row when the content copy fails' uses a source with `fileId: null`, so `discardBlob` is a no-op there and only `deleteDocument` is asserted. A file-backed document whose content copy fails (leaking the copied blob) has no coverage.

samples.summary: Nothing asserts the Yorkie `docKeyPrefix` (or that source and target share it)
samples.evidence: The mock `withDocument` in the spec branches only on `opts.syncMode` and ignores `opts.docKeyPrefix`; no test inspects the options argument. A wrong or mismatched prefix — reading the source under one key and writing the copy under another, which would silently produce an empty copy in production — cannot fail any of these tests.

samples.summary: `copyDocument` controller tests omit the non-member rejection case
samples.evidence: `describe('DocumentController.copyDocument')` covers 404 and the plain-member allow path, but no case where `assertMember` rejects; nothing proves the membership gate is awaited before `copyService.copy` runs (a reordering that copied first and checked later would still pass both existing tests, since the happy path's assertMember resolves).
searchedFor: read the copyDocument describe block in the diff

samples.summary: `copyTitle` test 'only considers the titles it is given' asserts nothing new
samples.evidence: `expect(copyTitle('Report', [])).toBe('Report (copy)')` is a weaker restatement of the first test (`['Report']` → 'Report (copy)'). Its comment claims folder/workspace scoping, but `copyTitle` has no notion of folders — the scoping lives in `DocumentCopyService`, so this case cannot fail for the reason it documents.

samples.summary: Length clamping is only tested for the unnumbered ` (copy)` suffix
samples.evidence: The clamp test uses a 200-char base whose ` (copy)` candidate is free. No case covers a clamped title whose ` (copy)` form is taken and must fall through to ` (copy 2)`+ — the interaction between truncation and the numbering loop (where different suffix lengths change the truncated base) is untested.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as described. The only 'doc'-arm test (document-copy.service.spec.ts:117-123) builds the service with an empty source root, so readDocsRoot returns {blocks: []} (docs-tree.ts:427-431) and writeDocsRoot then unconditionally seeds root.content = new Tree(...) (docs-tree.ts:517-528). The assertion `expect(targetRoot.content).toBeDefined()` therefore holds regardless of whether any source content was read or transferred; it only discriminates the routing (that a write happened at all), not the content copy in document-copy.service.ts:134-153. No other test copies real docs content: DocumentCopyService is only referenced by this spec and by document.controller.spec.ts where it is a bare jest.fn() mock (lines 13, 109, 193, 321), and there is no copy e2e test in packages/backend/test. docs-tree.spec.ts round-trips the serializer in isolation but exercises none of the copy wiring. This is fake coverage for a new behavior — major under the test-adequacy rubric.

verdict.reason: Verified against the repo. `copyContent` in packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts:129-199 has three arms: `doc` (134-153), `note` (155-174, using yorkieDocKeyPrefix('note') + readNoteRoot/writeNoteRoot), and the JSON_ROOT_TYPES snapshot path (176-198). Reading document-copy.service.spec.ts in full (1-193), the only `service.copy` invocations use type 'sheet' (SOURCE, line 8), 'doc' (line 119) and 'pdf' (lines 131, 157); there is no case with type 'note', and no assertion touches note content or the note key prefix. I searched wider than the reviewer: repo-wide grep for readNoteRoot/writeNoteRoot/copyContent (only note-content.ts/spec.ts, docs-content.controller, the copy service and design docs), repo-wide grep for DocumentCopyService/copyDocument/'/copy' (no e2e or integration test references — packages/backend/test/* contains no 'copy' match at all), and repo-wide grep of *.spec.ts/*.test.ts for 'note' literals. The nearest thing is packages/backend/src/yorkie/note-content.spec.ts, which unit-tests readNoteRoot/writeNoteRoot in isolation (lines 28-59) but never exercises the copy service's dispatch on type 'note' — so a regression that dropped or mis-prefixed the note arm (copying notes as empty) would still ship green. This is a shipped behavior branch with no covering test, i.e. a major missing-test finding in the test-adequacy lane.

verdict.reason: The claimed absence holds up. `copyDocument()` (packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:107-118) and the "Make a copy" UI wiring (packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-list.tsx:562-578 row menu at 982-990, bulk bar at 1201-1212) are new behavior with no frontend test. I read packages/frontend/src/api/documents.test.ts in full: it imports and covers only `moveDocuments` and `deleteDocuments` (lines 7, 15-44); `copyDocument` is not imported or exercised. Searching wide for a counterexample: repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `Make a copy|copyDocument|/copy` yields no frontend test file (only backend document-copy.service.spec.ts / document.controller.spec.ts, plus an unrelated docs-context-menu test that matches "Copy link"-style code); grep for the toast strings `copies created|Copy created|Failed to copy` matches only the two source files; a glob of all 152 frontend test files plus a `copy|Copy` grep across packages/frontend shows no hit in the plausible bulk-action tests (src/app/documents/__tests__/document-bulk.test.ts, tests/app/documents/document-list-utils.test.ts); there is no e2e/playwright/cypress suite in the repo; the hunt-ui scripts' "copy" matches are prose comments only. The feature's own task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260813-document-copy-todo.md:29) lists unit tests for the title util, copy service, and controller endpoint only — all backend. So the POST verb/URL, the sequential bulk loop, the singular/plural toast, and the deliberate onSettled-instead-of-onSuccess refetch on partial failure are all unverified, while sibling API functions in the same module are tested in the same file. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a clear behavior change shipped with no meaningful test — major.
